# Assignment 2
Lim Excelyynx (34476245)

## Approach

My approach on completing Assignment 2 is by cleaning the dataset as I work through each question, rather than cleaning entire dataset prior to starting question 1. This ensures that i respect question-specific constraints.

## Handling odd data values

I am aware that the dataset contains unsensible values (eg: negative, NA, unformatted). This will be cleaned by making them consistent as described in Assignment2 brief as I work through each question.

### Load tidyverse
```{R}
library(tidyverse)
```

### Load and save Wastes.csv and Year_State_ID.csv

```{R}
waste <- read_csv("data/Wastes.csv")
waste

year_state_id <- read_csv("data/Year_State_ID.csv")
year_state_id
```

## 1. Number of unique "Category" values in Wastes.csv

```{R}
# observe unique category
waste %>%
  select(Category) %>%
  distinct(Category)

# we observe the following:
# 1. "Building and demolition materials" and "Building & demolition materials" is category
# 2. "Hazardous wastes" and "HW" is the same category
# 3. "Plastics" and "Plastic" is the same category
# 4. "Organics" and "organics" is the same category
# 5. NA category is present
waste_unique <- waste %>%
  filter(!is.na(Category)) %>%
  mutate(
    Category = str_replace_all(Category, "&", "and"),
    Category = str_replace_all(Category, "HW", "Hazardous wastes"),
    Category = str_replace_all(Category, "^Plastic$", "Plastics"),
    Category = str_replace_all(Category, "organics", "Organics")
  )

# observe new unique category
# NA has been removed, "&" is replace with "and", "HW" is replace with "Hazardous Waste", "Plastic" is replace with "Plastics"
waste_unique %>%
  select(Category) %>%
  distinct(Category)

# get each distinct values in Category column and count total row
number_unique_wastes_category <- waste_unique %>% 
  distinct(Category) %>%
  nrow()

number_unique_wastes_category
```

## 2. Number of negative feedback comments in the 'Description' column with an environmental impact score of 2 or 3

### Observe the patterns of values of Description column
```{R}
waste_unique %>% select("Description")
```

### Sentence structure 
Description: "... Environmental Impact Score: 6/10 ...". Extract the value from "value/10" into a new column Env_Impact_Score
```{R}
waste_unique <- waste_unique %>%
  mutate(Env_Impact_Score = str_extract(Description, "Environmental Impact Score: \\d+") %>%
           str_extract("\\d+") %>%
           as.numeric()
  )
```

### Filter and count row with Env_Impact_Score value 2-3
```{R}
number_negative_env_impact_score <- waste_unique %>% 
  filter(Env_Impact_Score %in% c(2,3)) %>%
  nrow()

number_negative_env_impact_score
```

## 3. Calculate the fractions of waste tonnes of different waste sources, draw a chart to visualize the fraction numbers specific to the Category value

### Observe Stream column
```{R} 
waste_unique %>% 
  select(Stream) %>%
  distinct(Stream)
```

### Clean Stream column:
1. "Construction and demolition waste" should be "C&I"
2. "Municipal solid waste"  should be "MSW"
3. NA value should be removed
```{R}
waste_unique <- waste_unique %>%
  mutate(Stream = str_replace_all(Stream, "Construction and demolition waste", "C&D"),
         Stream = str_replace_all(Stream, "Municipal solid waste", "MSW")) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(Stream))

waste_unique
```

### Clean Tonnes column
1. Remove Tonnes that are NA
2. Remove Tonnes <= 0
```{R}
waste_unique <- waste_unique %>%
  filter(!is.na(Tonnes)) %>%
  filter(Tonnes > 0)

waste_unique %>% select(Tonnes)
```

### Calculate waste fraction
```{R}
waste_fraction <- waste_unique %>%
  group_by(Category, Stream) %>%
  summarise(stream_tonnes = sum(Tonnes, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(Category) %>%
  mutate(
    category_total = sum(stream_tonnes),
    fraction = stream_tonnes / category_total
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

waste_fraction
```

### Draw chart visualizing the fraction numbers specific to the Category value
```{R}
ggplot(waste_fraction, aes(x = Category, y = fraction, fill = Stream)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  labs(
    title = "Fraction of Waste Tonnes by Source within each Category",
    x = "Category",
    y = "Fraction of Tonnes",
    fill = "Stream"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

```

## 4. Add the 'Year' and 'State' values from Year_State_ID.csv to Wastes.csv, compute the total waste tonnes for each year and state, and store the result in a dataset named 'temp', compute and display the statistical information (min, max, mean) of the total waste tonnes for each state in ‘temp’

### Clean waste:
1. Remove all NA values
2. Remove non-sensible Tonnes values (<= 0)
3. Consistent Category values
4. Consistent Stream values
5. Extract Env_Score column from Description (IDK NEED MA)
```{R}
finalised_waste <- waste %>%
  filter(!is.na(Category) & !is.na(Stream) & !is.na(`Core_Non-core`) & !is.na(Tonnes)) %>%
  filter(Tonnes > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    Category = str_replace_all(Category, "&", "and"),
    Category = str_replace_all(Category, "HW", "Hazardous wastes"),
    Category = str_replace_all(Category, "^Plastic$", "Plastics"),
    Category = str_replace_all(Category, "organics", "Organics")
  ) %>%
  mutate(Stream = str_replace_all(Stream, "Construction and demolition waste", "C&D"),
         Stream = str_replace_all(Stream, "Municipal solid waste", "MSW")) %>%
  mutate(Env_Impact_Score = str_extract(Description, "Environmental Impact Score: \\d+") %>%
           str_extract("\\d+") %>%
           as.numeric()
  )

finalised_waste
```

### Left-join year_state_id to finalised_waste. 
Resulting temp table has:
1. Year
2. State
3. Total_Waste_Tonnes
```{R}
temp <- finalised_waste %>%
  left_join(year_state_id, by = c("Year_State_ID" = "ID")) %>%
  select(-Economic_Growth) %>%
  mutate(State = str_to_upper(State)) %>%
  group_by(Year, State) %>%
  summarise(Total_Waste_Tonnes = sum(Tonnes, na.rm = TRUE))

temp
```

### Summary (min, max, mean) of each state
The temp_state_summary has:
1. State
2. Min
3. m\Mean
4. Max
```{R}
temp_state_summary <- temp %>%
  group_by(State) %>%
  summarise(
      Min = min(Total_Waste_Tonnes, na.rm = TRUE),
      Mean = mean(Total_Waste_Tonnes),
      Max = max(Total_Waste_Tonnes, na.rm = TRUE))

temp_state_summary
```

## 5. Yearly trend of total waste tonnes of food organics for each state

### Format year
```{R}
year_formatted <- finalised_waste %>%
  left_join(year_state_id, by = c("Year_State_ID" = "ID")) %>%
  mutate(State = str_to_upper(State)) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.numeric(str_extract(Year, "^\\d{4}")))

year_formatted 
```

### Filter food organics
The food_organics_waste table has:
1. Year
2. State
3. Food_Organics_Tonnes
```{R}
food_organics_waste <- year_formatted %>%
  filter(Type %in% c("Food organics")) %>%
  group_by(Year, State) %>%
  summarise(Food_Organics_Tonnes = sum(Tonnes, na.rm = TRUE))

food_organics_waste
```

### Plot food organics by year
```{R}
ggplot(food_organics_waste, aes(x = Year, y = Food_Organics_Tonnes, color = State)) + 
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() + 
  labs(
    title = "Yearly Treand of Food Organics Waste Tonnes by State",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Total Food Organics Waste (Tonnes)",
    color = "State"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


```

## 6. Display the most recycled waste Type and the most energy-recovered waste Type with the corresponding year. Display the most increased waste Type over years

### Waste with recycling as Fate
```{R}
fate_recycling <- year_formatted %>% 
  filter(Fate %in% c("Recycling"))

fate_recycling
```

### Sum per year of each waste type with recycling as Fate
The recycled_waste_type table has:
1. Type
2. Year
3. Recycled_Tonnes
```{R}
recycled_waste_type <- fate_recycling %>%
  group_by(Type, Year) %>%
  summarise(Recycled_Tonnes = sum(Tonnes, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

recycled_waste_type
```

### Most recycled waste type
```{R}
most_recycled_waste_type <- recycled_waste_type %>%
  filter(Recycled_Tonnes == max(Recycled_Tonnes))

most_recycled_waste_type
```

### Waste with energy-recovered as Fate
```{R}
fate_energy_recovery <- year_formatted %>%
  filter(Fate %in% c("Energy recovery"))

fate_energy_recovery
```

### Sum per year of each waste type with energy-recovered as Fate
The energy_recovered_waste_type table has:
1. Type
2. Year
3. Energy_Recovered_Tonnes
```{R}
energy_recovered_waste_type <- fate_energy_recovery %>%
  group_by(Type, Year) %>%
  summarise(Energy_Recovered_Tonnes = sum(Tonnes, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

energy_recovered_waste_type
```

### Most energy-recovered waste type
```{R}
most_energy_recovered_waste_type <- energy_recovered_waste_type %>%
  filter(Energy_Recovered_Tonnes == max(Energy_Recovered_Tonnes))

most_energy_recovered_waste_type
```

### Find first and last year data of each waste type
The yearly_waste_type has:
1. Type
2. First_Year
3. Last_Year
4. First_Tonnes
5. Last_Tonnes
6. Change
```{R}
yearly_waste_type <- year_formatted %>%
  group_by(Type, Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Tonnes = sum(Tonnes, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Type) %>%
  summarise(
    First_Year = min(Year),
    Last_Year = max(Year),
    First_Tonnes = Total_Tonnes[Year == min(Year)],
    Last_Tonnes = Total_Tonnes[Year == max(Year)],
    Change = Last_Tonnes - First_Tonnes
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

yearly_waste_type
```

### Most incremented waste type
```{R}
most_incremented_waste_type <- yearly_waste_type %>%
  filter(Change == max(Change))

most_incremented_waste_type  
```

## 7. Investigate the factors influencing environmental impact scores

### Environmental Impact Score distribution
```{R}
ggplot(finalised_waste, aes(x = Env_Impact_Score)) + geom_bar()
```

### Is category a factor?
Observation:
- Toxic waste has lowest Mean_EIS
- Aluminium, Glass, Paper and cardboard has highest Mean_EIS
```{R}
category <- finalised_waste %>%
  group_by(Category) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_EIS = mean(Env_Impact_Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_EIS = sd(Env_Impact_Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Count = n()
) %>% arrange(Mean_EIS)

category

ggplot(category, aes(x = reorder(Category, Mean_EIS), y = Mean_EIS)) + 
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Mean EIS by Category",
    x = "Category",
    y = "Mean EIS"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

finalised_waste %>% arrange(Category, Fate) %>% select(Category, Fate, Stream)
```

### State and Env_Impact_Score across the years

```{R}
state_score_summary <- finalised_waste %>%
  left_join(year_state_id, by = c("Year_State_ID" = "ID")) %>%
  mutate(
    State = str_to_upper(State),
    Year = as.numeric(str_extract(Year, "^\\d{4}"))

  group_by(Year, State) %>%

    Mean_EIS = mean(Env_Impact_Score, na.rm = TRUE),
```

### State, Economic_Growth and Env_Impact_Score across the years
```{R}
state_econ_score_summary <- finalised_waste %>%
  left_join(year_state_id, by = c("Year_State_ID" = "ID")) %>%
  mutate(
    State = str_to_upper(State),
    Year = as.numeric(str_extract(Year, "^\\d{4}"))
  ) %>%
  group_by(Year, State, Economic_Growth) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_EIS = mean(Env_Impact_Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = n()
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(Year)

state_econ_score_summary

# convert state_econ_score_summary to Year, State, Metric (Mean_EIS, Economic_Growth), Value
state_econ_long <- state_econ_score_summary %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Mean_EIS, Economic_Growth),
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

state_econ_long

ggplot(state_econ_long, aes(x = Year, y = Value, color = Metric)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() + 
  facet_grid(Metric ~ State, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Mean EIS and Economic Growth by State over Years",
    x = "Year",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
```
